COURSE OBJECTIVES & OUTCOMES

Learning Objectives

Upon completing this virtual laboratory experiment, learners will be able to:

  • 1. Understand Asymmetric Cryptography: Differentiate symmetric ciphers from asymmetric key exchange systems that eliminate the shared secret distribution problem.
  • 2. Master Key Pair Generation: Perform manual and automated calculations for modulus n, Euler's totient φ(n), coprime public exponent e, and modular inverse private exponent d.
  • 3. Comprehend Trapdoor One-Way Functions: Explain why factoring large composite numbers n = p × q is the computational foundation of RSA security.
  • 4. Execute Modular Exponentiation: Encrypt numeric plaintext keys using public key (e, n) and decrypt ciphertexts using private key (d, n).
  • 5. Validate Cryptographic Integrity: Verify that the recovered plaintext key matches the original input (M' ≡ M) with 100% accuracy.
